doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Jerome Richardson, Roy Haynes and Mingus
summary: How he knew Richardson, Haynes and Mingus from California before working with them in New York.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You started working with a great list of fellas. Jerome Richardson, Mingus, Roy Haynes. Were these like one night things kind of? Pick up gigs?
Well first of all Jerome Richardson, I knew him in California.
That’s right, he came from there too.

In fact we both lived in Berkeley. And I lived around the corner from him. So he got some groups together and we’d play weekends, whatever. And so I knew Jerome. Roy Haynes, I met him in California when he was with Sarah Vaughan, so when I came to New York we sort of hooked up together and worked some different things, trios, quartets. And Mingus, I knew him from California. In fact I worked with him in California, in San Francisco. He organized a small group, a quartet, and we opened up a new jazz club in San Francisco. It didn’t last long though, the club. Flopped quickly. And I made a couple of records with Mingus out there. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
